message.content:
Diagnose and FIX two related bugs in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine) that a fully-opted-in rehearsal run exposed. Edit only that file (and worker/migrate-detect.ts if a detection change is truly needed). After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` (green). Do NOT deploy/commit. Report root cause + fix with file:line for each.

## Evidence (from a real run, source 72.62.240.50, all opt-ins ON incl. MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA)
The source runs a CONTAINERIZED mongo (`mongo:8` container, e.g. `soulpilates-prod-mongo`) as part of compose projects. The log shows:
- `Detected MongoDB on the old server — taking a consistent dump (no torn datadir copy).`
- then FAILS: `Migrate MongoDB — MongoDB is running on the old server but mongodump is [not installed]`
- `Recreating 26 standalone container(s) from the old server.`  ← far too many; the compose containers appear to be recreated standalone too
- Backends (ports 8391/8491) and mongo (27117) never come up → sites don't serve (2/6).

## BUG 1 — the HOST mongo/redis dump path (F4) fires for a CONTAINERIZED engine and fails
The engine has TWO db-dump paths: F1 (containerized, `docker exec <container> mongodump/pg_dump/mysqldump` — the mongo:8 container HAS mongodump inside) and F4 (host-native, runs `mongodump`/`pg_dumpall` on the source HOST). Search `host-mongo`, `host-redis`, `Detected MongoDB`, `command -v mongod`, `/var/lib/mongodb`, `containerDbDumpScript`, `dbEngineInfo`, `restoreVolumes`.
Root cause to confirm: F4's host detection (`command -v mongod || /var/lib/mongodb present` — even after the earlier "require running/non-empty" tweak) is TRUE on this source (a host mongod binary/dir exists as leftover, OR the check is too loose), so F4 tries a HOST `mongodump` which isn't installed on the host → fails and reports the DB not migrated — even though the REAL mongo is the containerized one that F1 already dumps correctly via `docker exec`.
FIX: F4 (host mongo/redis) must NOT fire when the engine is actually running in a CONTAINER that F1 handles. Before F4 treats a host mongo/redis as the thing to migrate, exclude it when there's a RUNNING source container whose image is that engine (mongo/redis) — i.e. if `srcContainers` has a running `mongo`/`redis` image, the containerized F1 path owns it and F4 must skip (a leftover host binary/empty datadir is not the real DB). Only run the host path for a genuinely host-native engine with data AND no containerized instance. Verify F1 actually dumps the containerized mongo (`docker exec <c> mongodump --archive`) and restores it — trace that it runs for `soulpilates-prod-mongo`.

## BUG 2 — compose containers ALSO recreated as standalone ("Recreating 26 standalone")
The standalone recreation filter is `srcContainers.filter(c => !c.project && !underComposeDir(c))`. Compose containers carry `c.project`, so they SHOULD be excluded. But 26 are being recreated. Confirm why: are these compose containers whose `c.project` came back empty in THIS run? Or is `underComposeDir` not covering them? Or are they the source's containers whose compose project dir wasn't in `composeDirsAll` so they're treated as standalone despite having a project? 
Root-cause and FIX so a container that belongs to ANY compose project the engine is bringing up is NOT also recreated standalone (which causes name/port conflicts with the compose-managed one and wasted work). Likely: exclude any container whose `c.project` matches a project the engine `compose up`'d (build a set of the projects/dirs actually brought up, and filter standalone against it), in addition to the existing `!c.project`/`underComposeDir` checks. Ensure a genuinely-standalone `docker run` container is still recreated.

## Guardrails
- Do not break the working F1 containerized-DB dump/restore, F2 projArg, F3 empty-volume guard, or the compose bring-up. A container that is genuinely host-native or genuinely standalone must still be handled.
- Keep it read-only on the source; validate interpolated values; single-quoted `sh -c '…'`.
- Finish only when tsc clean + both tests pass. Report: F4-vs-F1 routing fix (how you detect "a containerized instance exists so skip host"), and the standalone-exclusion fix, each with file:line, and confirm F1 dumps the containerized mongo.

Both fixes are in, tsc is clean, and all 41 tests pass. Here is the report.

## Root cause + fix

### BUG 1 — host mongo/redis (F4) fires for a containerized engine and fails
**Root cause:** The F4 host-native block (`worker/migrate-real.ts`, section 8a, ~line 6252) decided a host DB existed from `mongoRunning = pgrep -x mongod …` / `redisRunning = pgrep -x redis-server …` plus a `/var/lib/mongodb` (`/var/lib/redis`) data check. Because Docker containers share the host PID namespace, the `mongod` process inside `soulpilates-prod-mongo` (image `mongo:8`) is **visible to a host `pgrep`**, so `mongoRunning` was TRUE. F4 then ran a HOST `mongodump` (not installed on the host) and reported "MongoDB is running… mongodump is not installed → data NOT migrated" — even though F1 had already dumped the real containerized mongo correctly via `docker exec … mongodump --archive`. A leftover host mongod binary/empty datadir would trigger the same false path.

**Fix** (`worker/migrate-real.ts:6263-6265`, applied at `:6274` and `:6338`): before the host path runs, detect a RUNNING source container whose image basename is `mongo`/`redis`:
```ts
const hasContainerisedMongo = srcContainers.some((c) => c.state === "running" && /mongo/.test(imgBaseName(c.image)));
const hasContainerisedRedis = srcContainers.some((c) => c.state === "running" && /redis/.test(imgBaseName(c.image)));
```
and gate the host path on it: `const hostMongo = (mongoRunning || mongoHasData) && !hasContainerisedMongo;` (redis analogous at `:6338`). When a containerized instance exists, F1 owns it and F4 skips entirely. A genuinely host-native engine (no containerized instance) still runs the host path unchanged.

**F1 confirmed** for the containerized mongo: step 7pre (`:6009-6040`) iterates running containers, `dbEngineInfo("mongo:8")` → engine `mongo`/datadir `/data/db`, finds the named-volume datadir mount, and runs `containerDbDumpScript` → `docker exec soulpilates-prod-mongo sh -c '… mongodump --archive …'` (`:2355-2360`). Its volume is registered in `restoreVolumes` (so the hot copy is skipped) and restored after bring-up at `:7530-7563` via `containerDbRestoreCommand` → `docker exec -i … mongorestore --archive --drop`.

### BUG 2 — compose containers also recreated as "standalone"
**Root cause:** The standalone filter was `srcContainers.filter(c => !c.project && !underComposeDir(c))`. On this source the compose containers came back with an **empty `c.project`** label (so `!c.project` was true), and a DB container like `soulpilates-prod-mongo` keeps its datadir in a **named volume**, not a bind mount — so `underComposeDir` (which only inspects bind-mount sources under compose dirs) missed it too. Result: 26 compose-owned containers fell through to standalone `docker run` recreation, clashing on name/port with the compose-managed ones and wasting work.

**Fix** (`worker/migrate-real.ts`):
- Accumulate the merged `container_name`s of every compose project brought up into a hoisted `composeOwnedNames` set (declared `:6831`, populated `:7097` right after the authoritative `names` are computed — before the clash/empty-volume guards can `continue`, so a refused project still owns its names).
- Tightened the standalone filter (`:7409-7411`) to also exclude a container whose compose working-dir label matches a dir being brought up (`composeWdOwned`, `:7401`) and, crucially, whose name is in `composeOwnedNames`:
```ts
const standalone = srcContainers.filter((c) =>
  !c.project && !underComposeDir(c) && !composeWdOwned(c) && !composeOwnedNames.has(c.name)
);
```
The name-ownership check is what catches the empty-project, named-volume mongo case. A genuine `docker run` container's name is not a compose `container_name`, so it stays out of the set and is still recreated.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean (exit 0).
- `npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts test/customer-actions-guards.test.ts` → 41 pass, 0 fail.
- Untouched: F1 dump/restore, F2 projArg, F3 empty-volume guards, compose bring-up. `worker/migrate-detect.ts` needed no change. Not deployed/committed.
